kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR17 e) 1.): 'The file position indicator is set to the value of the key of reference in the first logical record whose key satisfies the comparison'. IMPLEMENTATION: IndexedConnector.Start builds `IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord(keyIndex)` — records sorted by (key-of-reference value under IndexedConnector.OrderOf, then Arrival) with SUPPRESS WHEN records filtered out — then iterates FORWARD for '==','>','>=' and BACKWARD for '<','<=' (GR17 c/d) and stops at the first satisfying record, setting `_fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex)` (the key VALUE, as the rule states) plus `_fpiArrival` (the duplicate-key disambiguator 9.1.8.2 needs to make arrival-order retrieval work; it adds resolution, it does not contradict the rule). GR17 e)'s operand orientation is right: `IndexedConnector.OrderOf(part, value, keyIndex)` puts the RECORD'S extracted key on the left, matching 'with the second temporary area on the left hand side' (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK). The suppression sentence is honored by IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord's `Where(r => !IndexedConnector.AlternateValue(r.Image, keyIndex))`, and IndexedConnector.AlternateValue returns false for keyIndex < 0 so the prime key is never suppressible. The partial-key truncation uses the WITH LENGTH count when present, else the operand's ImageWidth (EmitStart). OBSERVED (probe/idx-start/STPRB3, keys AAA100/BBB200/CCC300): implicit EQUAL 'BBB200' -> BBB200; '> BBB200' -> CCC300; '< BBB999' -> BBB200 (the LARGEST key below, proving the reverse search); 'NOT GREATER BBB999' -> BBB200; '>= AAA000 WITH LENGTH 3' -> AAA100. probe/idx-dup/STPRBB (alternate key WITH DUPLICATES, MM written by 05, 03, 09 in that arrival order): '>= MM' positions at 05 — the EARLIEST arrival of the duplicate set, and the walk gives 05, 03, 09; '< NN' positions at 09 — the LATEST arrival, i.e. the first satisfying record in reverse order. TESTS: conformance:cases/12.4.5.7-COLLATING-SEQUENCE/file_collating_seq pins START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV (expected 'START >= M UNDER REV:' then K=M, K=A, derived from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, not from any oracle); conformance:cases/14.9.9-CONTINUE/altkey_suppress_when pins START KEY IS >= LOW-VALUES on a SUPPRESS-WHEN alternate key (expected 01/AA then 03/BB); conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition asserts GOT=01 for START KEY = via a sibling-record operand, reasoned from 12.4.5.12.4 GR4 + 14.9.41.3 SR6b. All three compute their expected values from the standard. EDITIONS: the GR17 e) suppression sentence depends on SUPPRESS WHEN, a COBOL-2023 addition (cite.py --check E.3.3 OK, item 42), and the WITH LENGTH count in GR17 b) is a post-85 phrase; the rule itself is present in every edition. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, on the same defect as GR9 and for the same reason: the record claims edition 85 for a branch COBOL-85 does not have and the compiler does not gate. The BEHAVIOUR survived everything I threw at it. I re-derived the ordering from source rather than from the notes: IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord (:510-513) sorts by (key-of-reference value under IndexedConnector.OrderOf, then Arrival) with IndexedConnector.AlternateValue filtered out, and Start (:444-481) walks seq[i] for '=='/'>'/'>=' and seq[Count-1-i] for '<'/'<=', which is exactly 9.1.8's reverse order (descending key, reverse arrival); IndexedConnector.OrderOf(part, value, keyIndex) puts the RECORD's extracted key on the left, matching GR17 e)'s 'second temporary area on the left hand side'; _fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex) is the key VALUE the rule names. I verified BOTH cited conformance goldens by reading them, not by trusting the note: 2002/file_collating_seq computes START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV -> 'K=M','K=A' from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, and 2023/altkey_suppress_when computes the SUPPRESS-WHEN skip from 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 -- both spec-derived, both genuinely pinning the FPI-setting branch (a mis-set FPI changes the printed walk). I then probed the edges neither test reaches. Nothing broke. What breaks is editions '85,2002,2014,2023': the record's own notes claim the BACKWARD arm for COBOL-85 ('iterates FORWARD for ==,>,>= and BACKWARD for <,<= ... < BBB999 -> BBB200, proving the reverse search'), and that operator set is A.3 item 39's other half of READ PREVIOUS, which the compiler does gate at 2002. On an indexed file the leak is starker than on a relative one: in ONE probe file the COLLATING SEQUENCE clause (2002) and SUPPRESS WHEN (2023) each correctly raise COBOL0900 at --std 85 while 'START IXF KEY IS LESS THAN R-KEY' beside them raises nothing. The gate exists for every neighbouring post-85 feature of this exact statement and not for this one. Forward arm verified at four editions and closed by two spec-derived tests; reverse arm verified at three editions and ungated at the fourth => PARTIAL.
